questions.q: What are the two S3 buckets this capstone's architecture is built around?
options: A single bucket with no separation between raw and processed data
questions.explain: northfield-raw-zone holds unmodified source files; northfield-curated-zone holds the Glue ETL job's cleaned Parquet output.

questions.q: Why does the raw zone use a Hive-style dt=2026-09-19/ partition key instead of a flat folder?
options: So Glue and Athena can infer date partitions automatically instead of scanning the entire bucket
Because CSV files cannot be stored without a partition key
It has no functional purpose, only cosmetic
questions.explain: Hive-style key=value partitioning (dt=2026-09-19) is recognized automatically by Glue crawlers and Athena, avoiding full-bucket scans.

questions.q: What does the northfield-glue-scripts bucket hold?
options: The versioned PySpark scripts the Glue ETL job runs, later deployed via CI/CD
questions.explain: northfield-glue-scripts holds the Glue job's source scripts — the deployment target for Lesson 11's CI/CD pipeline.

questions.q: What naming convention does this lesson establish for every resource in the project?
options: A consistent northfield- (or northfield_) prefix on every resource
Random unique IDs generated by AWS
Resources are named after AWS service codes only
No naming convention — names are decided ad hoc in each later lesson
questions.explain: Every resource — buckets, Glue jobs, Redshift objects, Step Functions, IAM roles — is prefixed northfield- so its ownership is obvious at a glance.

questions.q: In the full architecture diagram from this lesson, what triggers the Step Functions state machine on a schedule?
questions.explain: EventBridge fires northfield-pipeline-orchestrator on a nightly schedule, starting the crawler -> ETL -> Redshift COPY -> notification chain.
